# A tab dragged from its popup into main leaves its header proxy behind

## Context

Operator, 2026-10-23 ~17:28Z, his manual test of the v13.3.1 head (screenshot): after dragging the Audit tab out of a popup window back into the main window, the Audit **header drag proxy** stays painted in main, a floating "Audit" tab button over the pane that just landed (`style: left 1018px, top 595px`, 48×32).

The live app (his Chrome, Neural Link session `5d49aeee…`, dev 2bbedf0222) still holds the leak, read at 17:29–17:31Z:

- `find_instances` `Neo.draggable.DragProxyComponent`: one instance, `neo-dragproxy-5`, **mounted**, `hidden: false`, `parentId: document.body`, `windowId` = main (`45bb5ec4…`), cls `neo-tab-header-toolbar … neo-is-dragging … neo-dock-dragproxy workstation-vessel-dragproxy neo-dragproxy`, vdom: one `neo-tab-header-button` "Audit", `aria-selected`.
- `find_instances` `Neo.dashboard.dock.window.VesselProxyEmbodiment` (`neo-base-48`): **`active` = `{generation: 2, header: true, itemId: 'audit', promoted: false, settled: true, sourceWindowId: '03befbf8…' (the popup), targetWindowId: '45bb5ec4…' (main), proxy: neo-dragproxy-5}`**. A header-proxy generation that was neither promoted nor restored.
- Every `TabSortZone` in both windows: `dragProxy: null`, `isWindowDragging: false`, `remoteDropCommitted: false`: the source side is clean; the residue is the target-side embodiment.
- `get_window_topology`: main `45bb5ec4…` (1127×918) and the popup `03befbf8…` (320×240), which hosts two dock nodes: `workstation-vessel-tabs:metrics` (sort zone 7) and `tabs-audit-0` (sort zone 8). Main also holds a `tabs-audit-0` node (sort zone 9): the Audit pane landed in main.
- Console (`Window.onWindowConnect`): the popup `03befbf8…` connected at …459282, a vessel `025aae98…` at …465366 (gesture 2) and a vessel `85c41b10…` at …473528 (gesture 3); neither vessel is open now.
- `get_drag_trace`, gesture 3: zone `neo-dock-tab-sortzone-8` (the popup's `tabs-audit-0` strip), item `neo-tab-header-button-26`, started …473395, a single `end from 0 to 0, noop` at …479157 and no move events (the moves ran in the other window). `get_drag_state`: every claim of `gesture-3` `claimed` **`workstation-main`**, the popup skipped as `source-or-excluded`; `abandonedGestures` empty; no console error.

So the gesture was: Audit's tab dragged out of the Metrics popup's strip, a tear-out vessel (`85c41b10…`) born 133 ms in, the drag carried into main, main claimed it, the drop committed (the pane is in main, the vessel closed), and the header proxy main had opened for the hover was left as the embodiment's live generation.

Sweeps: the newest 20 open issues at 17:30Z, no equivalent; title search "drag proxy" across all states: #19775 (closed 10-15 by PR #19779, the pane-proxy twin of this), #16623, #16117, #16120, #18020 (other proxy defects, closed); A2A claims of the last hour: none on this surface; Memory Core: my own 10-15 probe of #19775 (the two silent gates below).

## The Problem

`VesselProxyEmbodiment` opens one target-local proxy generation per cross-window hover (`openProxy`, `:211`) and retires it on exactly one of three terminals: `promote` after a commit (`:333`), `restore` on leave / refusal (`:376`), or `restoreByWindow` when either participating window departs (`:394`). All three resolve the record through `resolveRecord({itemId, sourceWindowId, targetWindowId})` (`:353-365`), which matches the **active** record by item and by the two window ids the caller supplies, and returns null on any mismatch. A header record (`record.header`) skips the inner `VesselEmbodiment` promote / restore and goes straight to `retireProxy`, so for a header proxy the only way to end with `promoted: false` and a mounted proxy is that **none of the three terminals resolved the record**.

#19775 (10-15) was the pane-proxy shape of this: the vessel's close ran the leave path before the commit settled, the leave's restore was refused, and `DragTarget`'s settle skipped the promote because the payload was no longer current. PR #19779 fixed that path for the gesture it reproduced (one popup, one main). Today's gesture has a third window: the Audit tab's own tear-out vessel, born from the popup mid-drag and closed after the commit. The record was opened with `sourceWindowId` = the popup (`03befbf8…`), the window the strip lived in; if the payload the commit and the leave carried names the vessel (`85c41b10…`) as the source, `resolveRecord` matches nothing, `promote` and `restore` return false, `restoreByWindow(85c41b10…)` matches neither side of the record, and the generation outlives its gesture with `promoted: false`, exactly the live state. That is the hypothesis the live record supports; the fix confirms it from the payload the coordinator built for gesture 3 (`DragCoordinator#commitNativeWindowDrop`, `:482-650`) and from `DragTarget#onRemoteDrop`'s `settle` (`:444-500`: promote only while `current || orphaned`).

What the user sees: a dead tab button floating over the pane until a reload; it reads as a stuck drag.

## The Architectural Reality

- `src/dashboard/dock/window/VesselProxyEmbodiment.mjs`: `openProxy` `:211-316`, `promote` `:333-346` (header records skip the inner promote), `resolveRecord` `:353-365` (identity = item + two window ids, **no generation**), `restore` `:376-388`, `restoreByWindow` `:394-401`, `retireProxy` `:408-420`, `snapshot` `:427-449`, `whenSettled` `:462+`.
- `src/dashboard/dock/window/DragTarget.mjs`: the owner seams `stageDragEmbodiment` / `promoteDragEmbodiment` / `restoreDragEmbodiment` / `isDragEmbodimentLive` `:108-163`, `onRemoteDragLeave` `:401-411` (a refused restore joins `#unrestoredPayloads`), `onRemoteDrop` `:444-500` (the settle's `current || orphaned` gate), `destroy` `:520-529`.
- `src/manager/DragCoordinator.mjs`: `clearNativeWindowDropCandidate` `:219`, `commitNativeWindowDrop` `:482-650` (the payload's window ids), `abandonNativeDrop` `:391`.
- `apps/workstation/view/VesselWorkspace.mjs:280-281`: the `neo-dock-dragproxy workstation-vessel-dragproxy` cls the leaked proxy wears, the Workstation's embodiment config.
- Prior art: #19775 / PR #19779 (the pane-proxy leak, same seam), #19248 (Ada's header proxy embodiment), #19797 (a returned vessel closes when main adopts), #16498 (the resident-card epic these sit under).

Design authority: `VesselProxyEmbodiment`'s own contract (`:18`: "It owns its proxies … and destroys both"), scene 2's cleanup contract that forbids residue (#19775's `:2456` read), and `promote`'s description ("the proxy is retired"). A generation must end at the gesture's terminal, whichever window carried the payload.

## The Fix

Make every terminal reach the generation it ends, with the window a gesture crossed into no longer able to hide the record:

1. Bind the record to the gesture, not to a window pair: `openProxy` records the coordinator's gesture token (or the generation id the payload carries) and `resolveRecord` matches on item + gesture when the identity carries one, falling back to the window pair only for callers that have none; `restoreByWindow` also retires a record whose gesture's **vessel** departed (the third window), not only its source or target.
2. Or, if the coordinator can keep the payload's `sourceWindowId` stable across a mid-gesture tear-out (the strip's window, as the record was opened), fix it there: one identity for one gesture. The builder picks from the payload trace; the AC does not care which.
3. A terminal that still resolves no record logs it (`console.error`, the e2e `workerErrors` gate's shape, like `reportAbandonedGesture`): a live generation with no owner is a defect, never silence.

Red-first: a unit arm over `VesselProxyEmbodiment` + `DragTarget` with a header record opened under (item, popup → main) and a commit whose payload names a different source window: today the record survives with `promoted: false`; after, it is retired. An e2e arm in `test/playwright/e2e/workstation/` performing the operator's gesture (Metrics torn out into a popup; Audit docked into that popup as its own node; Audit dragged from the popup's strip into main and dropped): today `find_instances` of `DragProxyComponent` after the drop is non-empty and the embodiment's `snapshot` shows a visible generation; after, both are empty and the Audit pane is in main.

## Decision Record impact

`none`.

## Measured Mechanism (2026-10-23)

The window-pair hypothesis above does not hold for this gesture. A probe trace of the e2e arm on dev `2bbedf0222`:

- The pointer drag's `draggedItem` is the popup's tab header **Button**, not the pane. Its frames carry no `sourceWindowId`, so `resolveRecord` checks only item and target, and the target (main) matches.
- The drop commits through `VesselWorkspace#commitCrossWindowTransfer`, which settles after the popup's projection. That projection removes Audit's tab and destroys the Button; `Base.destroy` deletes its own keys, so at the settle `Participation#getDragEmbodimentIdentity` reads `itemId: undefined`.
- `promote` resolves nothing and the header generation stays `promoted: false, settled: true, visible: true`, the live record above. No later terminal reaches it: the riding vessel's release matches neither window of the record, and is no terminal of the gesture anyway.

So the identity has to be the one the frame staged under, not one re-read from a component the drop itself destroys. AC-1 is restated to this mechanism; AC-2 to AC-4 stand.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1 **Unit, red-first:** a header-proxy generation staged for (item, popup → main) is retired by its committed drop although the dragged tab component was destroyed before the commit settled; on dev the generation stays live (`snapshot` visible, `promoted: false`). The pane-proxy arms of #19779 stay green. *(Restated 2026-10-23 from "a commit whose payload names the gesture's vessel as its source window, and by that vessel's departure", per the measured mechanism.)*
- [ ] AC-2 **E2E, the operator's gesture, red-first:** tear Metrics out into a popup, dock Audit into that popup, drag Audit from the popup's strip into main and drop: on dev a `DragProxyComponent` with `workstation-vessel-dragproxy` is mounted in main after the drop and the embodiment's `snapshot` reports a visible generation; on the head neither exists, the Audit pane is in main, the vessel is closed, no console error.
- [ ] AC-3 **No silent orphan:** with the fix's path forced to miss (a mocked identity that resolves nothing), the terminal logs an error naming item, generation and terminal; the e2e `workerErrors` gate reds on it.
- [ ] AC-4 **Live (PMV):** the operator repeats his gesture on the merged head and no header proxy stays.

## Out of Scope

- The pane-proxy path (#19779's fix stands).
- The vessel's close timing (#19797).
- Removing the leaked proxy from the operator's running app: a reload clears it; the live record is the evidence until then.

## Avoided Traps

- **Hiding the proxy on the next drag start:** a reset at the next gesture would mask the terminal that failed and leave the generation accounting wrong (#19775's lesson: a missed retire, not an orphan).
- **A generation-less identity (today):** two windows name a hover, not a gesture; a tear-out mid-gesture changes the window pair under the record.
